top_matches.release_note: (reliability) If your workspace did not allow messages to be copied, we were also erroneously preventing you from viewing file attachments. Here's a message we're not just copying from previous bug fixes: We're sincerely sorry for the trouble.

top_matches.release_note: (security) Fixed: Uploading a new profile picture was sometimes failing, leaving people stuck with their old ones like an unfortunate driver's license photo. Contrary to popular belief, we've never aspired for Slack to feel like going to the DMV, so retake that photo to your heart's content.
top_matches.review: (security) Profile picture never updates on this app.

top_matches.release_note: (efficiency) Fixed: Attempting to change your notification settings for a specific channel would routinely fail. Not in an entertaining way, or the sort that teaches you something important on your way to greater heights. It just didn't do the thing it was designed to do. Sometimes misfortune carries with it no lesson. Anyway, it works again.

(reliability) Fixed: When a message was deleted, it would very occasionally linger in the mobile app longer than was appropriate. See here, deleted messages: No lingering, loitering, dawdling, dithering or dallying. (Slack penal code 22.05.10)

(reliability) Fixed: We've removed the option to mention @here or @channel within a direct message. In the context of a DM, these mentions were superfluous, redundant, duplicative. Oh, and they also caused the app to crash spectacularly. So that wasn't great. Every message in a DM generates a notification just like an @mention, so all you need are your wonderful words.

bottom_matches.release_note: (usability) We do these releases every week to keep on top of performance ... but sometimes there's nothing specific to tell you. So let's talk about some things we could have mentioned more in the first place. Like, did you know that you can long-press on a message on mobile to set it to "unread," so it's there waiting for you when you get to your desk? Or set a reminder to look at it later? Oh, you did? Never mind, then. Carry on.
